skills.name: Tools of analysis: axes, graphs and scales

note.text: A graph represents relationships visually. Axes must be labelled with variables and units. A scale states the value represented by equal spaces. Points show paired observations. In a conventional demand diagram, quantity is on the horizontal axis and price on the vertical axis; the convention should be stated rather than guessed. A change in a graph can be misread if an axis is truncated or intervals are unequal. Use labels before interpreting height or slope.

sections.heading: Understand the ideas
sections.text: A graph represents relationships visually. Axes must be labelled with variables and units. A scale states the value represented by equal spaces. Points show paired observations. In a conventional demand diagram, quantity is on the horizontal axis and price on the vertical axis; the convention should be stated rather than guessed. A change in a graph can be misread if an axis is truncated or intervals are unequal. Use labels before interpreting height or slope.

sections.heading: Apply the ideas locally
sections.text: Ngozi compares weekly basket sales with a bar chart. The horizontal axis identifies the weeks and the vertical axis counts baskets. If one marked interval represents several baskets, the height must be read using that scale. A taller bar is not automatically more revenue: revenue also depends on the price charged.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Read the title, both axis labels and the scale. Follow a point or bar to the correct axis, then include the unit. Do not treat a category label as a numerical measurement. If a graph and its table disagree, identify which plotted point or label needs checking.
